headline: ChatGPT adds a Pro tier at $200 a month
details: OpenAI announced ChatGPT Pro as a new $200-per-month subscription tier on December 5, 2024. TechCrunch reported that it includes unlimited access to OpenAI's models, the full o1 model and o1 pro mode, and is ten times the cost of ChatGPT Plus.

headline: Zapier moves Starter users to Professional and adds 750 and 1,500 task tiers
details: From April 2, 2024, Zapier upgraded Starter customers to Professional at no extra cost, added 750 and 1,500 task tiers to Professional, and phased out the Company plan in favor of a new Enterprise plan. Paths, Filter and Formatter steps no longer count as tasks.

headline: Canva Teams jumps from $119.99 to $500 a year for some older plans
details: Fortune reported on September 3, 2024 that some Canva Teams subscribers on an older plan would move from $119.99 to $500 a year in early December (a U.S. example), with the first 12 months at $300. Teams customers who joined since April 2024 were already on the updated rates.

headline: Fivetran moves volume tiers to the connection level and ends Starter plan
details: From March 1, 2025, Fivetran applies monthly-active-row tiering per connection instead of per account, marks identical re-synced rows as free, bases annual contract discounts on commitment level, and no longer offers the Starter and Private Deployment plans. Fivetran said the change is calibrated to be neutral for the typical user.

headline: Power BI Pro rises from $10 to $14 per user a month
details: According to The Register and RCP Magazine, Power BI Pro went from $10 to $14 and Premium Per User from $20 to $24 per user a month, effective April 1, 2025. Existing customers keep the previous pricing until their contract renewal, and Power BI bought through Microsoft 365 E5 is unaffected.

headline: Anthropic launches Claude Max at $100 and $200 a month
details: Anthropic introduced Claude Max on April 9, 2025, according to CNBC and Maginative: a $100-a-month tier with five times the usage of the $20 Claude Pro plan, and a $200-a-month tier with twenty times.

headline: Notion bundles unlimited Notion AI into Business and Enterprise plans
details: On May 13, 2025, Notion said the Business and Enterprise plans now include unlimited Notion AI, with all-in-one pricing starting at $20 per user a month. Updated pricing applied to new subscriptions that day; for existing customers it starts at the first renewal after August 13, 2025.

headline: Figma moves to one seat per user and raises Full seat prices
details: Starting March 11, 2025, Figma migrates paid plans to Full, Dev, Collab and View seats, one seat per user. Figma said Full seat price increases and prorated billing changes apply at the first renewal on or after March 11, 2025; the free Starter plan continues.

headline: Airtable stops billing AI per seat and adds credits to Team and Business
details: Starting June 24, 2025, Airtable no longer charges for AI on a per-seat basis on Team and Business plans. Team plans get 15,000 monthly AI credits per billable collaborator and self-serve Business plans get 20,000 per paid user; unused add-on time is credited to the next invoice.

headline: Slack Business+ rises from $12.50 to $15 per user a month on annual billing
details: In its June 17, 2025 announcement, Slack said Business+ pricing increases from $12.50 to $15 per user a month on annual billing and from $15 to $18 on monthly billing. Pro pricing stays the same. Customers who bought on Slack's website move to the new Business+ at their first renewal after August 17, 2025.
unit: per user a month, billed annually

headline: Slack ends Slack AI add-on sales and puts AI summaries in all paid plans
details: With its June 2025 plan update, Slack said the Slack AI add-on is no longer available to buy on its website, and conversation summaries and huddle notes are included on all paid plans. Existing add-on buyers keep access until their first renewal after August 17, 2025; recaps and translations require Business+.

headline: QuickBooks Online Simple Start rises from $35 to $38 a month
details: According to Intuit's May 27, 2025 notice as relayed by accounting firms Woodard and BCS, QuickBooks Online monthly prices rose: Simple Start $35 to $38, Essentials $65 to $75, Plus $99 to $115, Advanced $235 to $275. Effective July 1, 2025 for client-billed subscriptions and August 1, 2025 for accountant-billed ones.

headline: Pipedrive replaces its plans with Lite, Growth, Premium and Ultimate
details: On July 15, 2025, Pipedrive announced new plans, Lite, Growth, Premium and Ultimate, replacing Essential, Advanced, Professional/Power and Enterprise. Pipedrive said switching to the best-matched plan means more features at the same cost for many existing customers, and switching to a new plan updates the subscription to Pipedrive's latest list pricing.

headline: Patreon replaces its 8% and 12% fees with a single 10% fee for new pages
details: For pages published after August 4, 2025, Patreon replaced its Pro (8%) and Premium (12%) plans with one standard plan that takes 10% of creator earnings. Creators who published before that date keep their existing rates, according to TechCrunch and Tubefilter.

headline: Loom raises prices for existing Business customers and ends Creator Lite
details: Atlassian said Loom is raising prices for its existing customer base for the first time, with Business and Business + AI customers advised to expect it as early as November 30, 2025, depending on each workspace's integration date. Creator Lite users are upgraded to paid Creator seats on that date; no price amounts are given.

headline: Anthropic lowers Claude Team prices to $20 and $100 a seat on annual billing
details: On January 28, 2026, Anthropic said it is lowering Claude Team prices. Standard seats are now $20 a month with annual discount or $25 billed monthly; Premium seats are $100 with a new annual discount or $125 monthly, and include five times the usage of Standard seats. The post does not list the previous prices.

headline: Backblaze B2 storage rises from $6 to $6.95 per TB a month
details: Announced March 17, 2026: from May 1 B2 Cloud Storage goes from $6/TB to $6.95/TB for pay-as-you-go customers, while API calls become free for all B2 customers. Existing committed contracts keep their price until renewal; B2 Reserve and Overdrive pricing is unchanged.

headline: ChatGPT adds a $100 Pro tier; $200 tier leaves the pricing page
details: TechCrunch reported on April 9, 2026 that OpenAI added a $100-a-month Pro tier with five times the Codex usage of Plus. The $200 Pro tier, with 20 times Plus limits, no longer appears on the pricing page, though OpenAI confirmed it is still available.

headline: Notion adds monthly AI credits to Business and Enterprise seats
details: On October 19, 2026, Notion said Business and Enterprise seats include 1,500 Standard and 500 Select credits a month, live for new customers that day. Existing customers move on November 2; admins can buy extra credits. The post lists no dollar prices.

headline: QuickBooks Online Essentials, Plus and Advanced rise to $85, $140 and $340 a month
details: Intuit said monthly prices for QuickBooks Online Essentials, Plus and Advanced change for renewals on or after August 1, 2026; Simple Start is unchanged. Its pricing page now lists $85, $140 and $340, against the $75, $115 and $275 set in July 2025. New subscribers keep their price for six months.

headline: Stripe Billing moves to one package at 0.7% of Billing volume
details: On July 10, 2024 Stripe replaced Billing Starter (0.5% of Billing volume) and Billing Scale (0.8%) with a single Stripe Billing package at 0.7% of Billing volume. Customers who were on the old plans kept a promotional 0.5% rate until June 30, 2025.

headline: Descript starts migrating legacy plans to new AI-credit plans
details: Descript said Legacy and Sunset plan subscribers are migrated automatically to its new plans, which use media minutes and a pool of AI credits, on their next billing date after November 17, 2025. Free users moved on September 23, 2025. The company said most customers will not see a price change, though some prices could increase.

headline: Google Workspace Business Standard rises from $12 to $14 per user a month
details: Google included Gemini in Workspace Business and Enterprise plans. Computerworld reported Business Standard rising from $12 to $14 per user a month on annual billing and Business Plus from $18 to $22; Google's blog confirms the $14 figure. New customers from January 16, 2025; existing monthly plans from March 17, 2025.
unit: per user a month, billed annually

headline: Webflow merges CMS and Business Site plans into Premium and adds a Team plan
details: Webflow combined its CMS and Business Site plans into one Premium Site plan ($25 a month billed yearly, $39 monthly) and added a Team plan. It said some customers will see an increase, some a decrease and some no change. New purchases from May 13, 2026; existing sites at their first renewal on or after June 29 or, for Freelancer, Agency and legacy-pricing sites, November 16, 2026.

headline: Eventbrite ends its Flex plan and upfront fees, returns to free publishing
details: In September 2024 Eventbrite discontinued its Flex plan (charged per event), removed upfront fees and again let creators publish events at no cost. The optional Pro subscription remains; Eventbrite's SEC filings say its price was reduced, without giving amounts.

headline: PostHog cuts session replay pricing; 25,000 recordings fall from $430 to $85
details: PostHog announced lower session replay pricing on July 23, 2024. Its examples: 25,000 recordings a month fall from $430 to $85 and 100,000 from $640 to $273. The 5,000 free recordings a month are unchanged, and existing customers were migrated to the new pricing.

headline: PostHog adds cheaper anonymous events to product analytics pricing
details: On August 1, 2024 PostHog announced separate pricing for identified and anonymous events in product analytics; until then every event was charged the same. Identified events cost the same as before; the company said anonymous events are between 55% and 80% cheaper for most customers and will soon become the default.

headline: PostHog data pipelines now bill by rows exported and trigger events
details: From September 11, 2025 PostHog bills data pipelines on rows exported and trigger events instead of all events ingested. The monthly free allowances are 10,000 trigger events and 1 million rows exported; usage up to the previous day was billed under the old scheme.

headline: Airbyte Cloud Standard rises from $10 to $20 a month; Plus gets new tiers
details: Announced September 15, 2026, Airbyte Standard's base price went from $10 to $20 a month on September 21, with free credits up from 4 to 5 and extra credits from $2.50 to $5.00. SSO is no longer on Standard (existing users keep it). New Plus plans include a 40-credit tier at $189; Pro and Flex are not affected.

headline: Kajabi raises prices on all plans; extra 5,000 contacts goes from $20 to $25
details: Kajabi announced a price increase across all plans; for existing customers the new pricing applies from their first billing date on or after January 13, 2026. Founder and Beta Invite plans are not affected. The extra 5,000 contacts price rises from $20 to $25. The company said it was its first price adjustment in 10 years.

headline: Phrase replaces per-product pricing with one platform subscription
details: From February 1, 2024 Phrase launched plans that include every platform capability under one subscription, instead of separate product licenses; Language Service Providers get a dedicated plan. Existing customers keep their arrangement until contract renewal unless they switch earlier.

headline: Foxit consolidates PDF Editor and eSign into four new options
details: Foxit announced PDF Editor, PDF Editor+ (with 150 eSign envelopes a year), eSign Essentials (250 envelopes a year) and eSign Business (unlimited). Existing eSign Pro and Enterprise customers are encouraged to move to eSign Business at renewal; switching is optional for others.

headline: Tableau stops selling Advanced Management and Data Management as add-ons
details: As of September 16, 2024 Tableau no longer sells Advanced Management or Data Management as independent add-ons. They remain available with Tableau Enterprise, Cloud+ or the Tableau+ Bundle (Data Management on Server: Enterprise or Server+), and only to customers who bought them earlier.

headline: Semrush launches Semrush One tiers, introductory pricing from $165 a month
details: On October 29, 2025 Semrush announced Semrush One in Starter, Pro+ and Advanced tiers, adding AI visibility tracking to its SEO data. Introductory pricing for new customers starts at $165 a month billed annually. The announcement does not say what happens to existing plans.

headline: Grammarly begins moving Premium subscribers to Pro at the same price
details: In March 2025 Grammarly began gradually migrating Premium users to its Pro plan, which includes everything in Premium plus twice the generative AI prompts (2,000 a month). Grammarly said billing amounts stay the same and it was not increasing the price at that time. Applies to Premium bought directly from Grammarly; App Store and Google Play subscribers are not affected.

headline: monday work management raises list prices by $1 to $3 per seat
details: monday.com said work management list prices become $9 for Basic (up $1), $12 for Standard (up $2) and $19 for Pro (up $3) per seat a month, billed annually. New subscriptions moved to the new prices on January 11, 2024 and existing customers on February 16, 2024.

headline: Smartsheet replaces its four tiers with a new member-based pricing model
details: Smartsheet said a new pricing and packaging model starts for new customers on June 24, 2024, replacing its four existing tiers and the paid editor and free collaborator model with licensed members. Existing customers move at their renewal dates in 2025. Per-member prices were not given in these sources.

headline: Auth0 Free plan limit rises from 7,500 to 25,000 monthly active users
details: In its plan update post, Auth0 wrote that on the new Free plan it increased the number of monthly active users from 7,500 to 25,000. Auth0 said the plan updates were available as of September 24, 2024.

headline: Microsoft 365 Personal, now with Copilot, rises from $6.99 to $9.99 a month (US)
details: Microsoft added Copilot to the US consumer plans Microsoft 365 Personal and Family and raised them by $3 a month. Per CNBC, Personal went from $6.99 ($69.99 a year) to $9.99 ($99.99) and Family from $9.99 to $12.99. Existing subscribers pay it at renewal and can switch to non-Copilot plans for a limited time.

headline: FlutterFlow replaces Standard, Pro and Teams with Basic, Growth and Business
details: FlutterFlow said new Basic, Growth and Business plans, with lower-cost single-seat options for Growth and Business, replace the Standard, Pro and Teams plans from August 18, 2025. Users had 30 days to choose; billing changes apply at the next renewal.

headline: Atlassian raises Jira Cloud list prices: Standard 5%, Premium 7.5%
details: Atlassian's investor notice says cloud list prices for Jira, Confluence, Jira Service Management and Teamwork Collection rose on October 15, 2025: Standard 5%, Premium 7.5%, Enterprise 7.5 to 10% by user count. Customers were notified August 19, 2025; impact phases in as subscriptions renew.

headline: Microsoft stops selling Copilot Pro and launches Microsoft 365 Premium at $19.99
details: Microsoft said it will no longer sell Copilot Pro, which PCWorld described as the $20 subscription, and offered Microsoft 365 Premium at $19.99 a month. Microsoft's support page says existing subscribers can keep using it until they cancel and that support ends on August 1, 2026.

headline: Teachable introduces Starter, Builder, Growth and Advanced plans
details: Teachable said new plans are available to new schools from the week of June 2, 2025. Builder, Growth and Advanced carry 0% base transaction fees (Builder was 5% on the old Basic plan) and Starter carries 7.5%. Existing schools were moved between June 15 and July 15, 2025.

headline: Voiceflow Business (formerly Teams) base price rises from $125 to $150 a month
details: Voiceflow moved to credits on April 29, 2025: Pro is $60 a month for 10k credits, Business (formerly Teams) rises from $125 to $150 for 30k credits, and extra editor seats are $50 a month. Annual plans shift from a 20% to a 10% discount; Starter is free with 100 credits.

headline: Botpress moves new workspaces to per-conversation pricing with unlimited bots
details: Botpress said it now charges per conversation instead of per incoming message, bundles AI spend into every plan and includes unlimited bots on paid plans. Listed prices: Plus $150, Team $750 a month. It applies only to workspaces created after May 14, 2026; legacy plans stay as they are for now.

headline: Firebase Cloud Storage now requires the paid Blaze plan; Spark loses bucket access
details: Google announced the change in September 2024. Its FAQ says Cloud Storage for Firebase, including default buckets, requires the pay-as-you-go Blaze plan, and that the requirement went into effect starting February 3, 2026. Projects on the no-cost Spark plan have no access to any buckets.

headline: Bettermode removes free plan communities by March 15, 2026
details: In its post introducing new Starter, Growth and Premium plans (the post shows no date), Bettermode said free plan communities will be removed by March 15, 2026; until then they can upgrade to a legacy plan or export content. Legacy plans change nothing until renewal.

headline: 1Password Individual annual price rises from $35.88 to $47.88
details: According to an email 1Password sent customers, as reported by 9to5Mac, annual Individual plans go from $35.88 to $47.88 a year for renewals on or after March 27, 2026. 9to5Mac and MacTrast list the annual Family plan at $71.88, up from $59.88.

headline: Google AI Plus drops from $7.99 to $4.99 a month and doubles storage to 400 GB
details: Google announced a price cut for AI Plus to $4.99 a month (or local equivalent) from the $7.99 US launch price, and storage rises from 200 GB to 400 GB. According to 9to5Google, the lower price applies from each subscriber's next renewal.

headline: Jira Cloud Standard (1-100 users, monthly) rises from $9.05 to $9.70 per user
details: Atlassian's cloud list price update took effect on October 13, 2026 PT and applies to new purchases as well as renewals and upgrades of existing subscriptions. Its tables show Jira monthly billing for 1-100 users: Standard $9.05 to $9.70, Premium $18.30 to $19.60 per user. Quotes issued before that date are honored at the prior price until they expire.
unit: per user a month (Standard, 1-100 users, monthly billing)

headline: Salesforce raises Enterprise and Unlimited Edition list prices by about 6%
details: Salesforce said list prices for Enterprise and Unlimited Editions of Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Field Service and select Industries Clouds would rise by an average of 6% on August 1, 2025. It said there were no planned price changes for Foundations, Starter or Pro Editions.

headline: Atlassian raises Confluence Cloud list prices: Standard 5%, Premium 7.5%
details: Atlassian's investor notice says cloud list prices for Confluence, Jira, Jira Service Management and Teamwork Collection rose on October 15, 2025: Standard 5%, Premium 7.5%, Enterprise 7.5 to 10% by user count. Customers were notified August 19, 2025; the notice says the impact is expected to phase in as subscriptions renew.

headline: Confluence Cloud Standard (1-100 users, monthly) rises from $6.70 to $7.15 per user
details: Atlassian's FAQ says new cloud list prices took effect October 13, 2026 PT for new purchases, renewals and upgrades. Its tables show Confluence monthly billing for 1-100 users: Standard $6.70 to $7.15, Premium $13.20 to $14.10 per user. Quotes issued before that date are honored at the prior price until they expire.
unit: per user a month (Standard, 1-100 users, monthly billing)

headline: Todoist raises Pro from $5 to $7 and Business from $8 to $10 a month on monthly billing
details: Todoist's help center says Pro goes from $5 to $7 a month ($4 to $5 billed yearly, $48 to $60 a year) and Business from $8 to $10 per user a month ($6 to $8 billed yearly). Each applies at the next renewal on or after December 10, 2025; App Store subscribers and Pro Legacy users are not covered.

headline: Clay cuts four paid plans to three: Launch from $185, Growth from $495, Enterprise
details: Clay's March 11, 2026 pricing memo gives every plan Data Credits and Actions and cuts marketplace data costs by 50 to 90%. The company compared Growth's $495 start with its legacy Pro plan ($800); its FAQ says the top-up premium falls from 50% to 30%. Existing customers can stay on legacy plans.

headline: Squarespace introduces Basic, Core, Plus and Advanced plans to replace legacy plans
details: Squarespace's February 25, 2025 post announced four website plans (Basic, Core, Plus, Advanced) to eventually replace Personal, Business, Commerce and Commerce Advanced. Existing customers can stay on legacy plans, but changing plan or billing cycle moves them to a new plan with no way back.

headline: Xero US Cashbook plan rises from $8 to $10 a month
details: Xero's notice says the price of Cashbook plans in the US rose from $8 to $10 a month on March 4, 2024, for new and existing plans. Xero Ledger and optional add-ons were unchanged, and existing discount or promo codes carry over until they expire.

headline: beehiiv adds a $99 Max plan; Scale starts at $39 and pricing follows subscriber count
details: beehiiv's April 18, 2024 post says the Scale plan is available at a lower price (starting at $39 a month), a new Max plan starts at $99, and pricing now depends on subscriber count. The Launch plan gained three features, and legacy Grow users move to Scale; some users whose price rises keep legacy pricing for several months.

headline: beehiiv renames plans to Free, Lite and Pro and sets seat and subscriber limits
details: From October 1, 2026 for new customers, beehiiv's Launch, Scale and Max become Free, Lite and Pro. Pro allows up to 250,000 subscribers and 10 team seats, Lite up to 100,000 subscribers and 2 seats, and every plan includes podcasts, community and digital products. Existing customers keep current rates until a renewal on or after November 1, 2026.

headline: Clerk raises its free tier from 10,000 monthly users to 50,000 monthly retained users
details: Clerk's pricing article says it ran a 10,000-user free tier from December 2023 until February 2026, and on February 5, 2026 raised the free allotment to 50,000 monthly retained users (MRU). It describes MRU as a narrower unit than monthly active users.

headline: Klaviyo email plans must now cover the account's active profile count
details: Klaviyo's billing changes took effect on February 18, 2025 for customers who pay by credit card: an email plan must cover the account's active profile count, and accounts over their profile limit move up a plan automatically. Free accounts are not upgraded automatically; flexible sending and auto-downgrade options were added to billing preferences.

headline: Make replaces operations with credits as its billing unit
details: Effective August 27, 2025, Make replaced operations with credits as its billing unit. Existing operation balances were converted to credits at a 1:1 ratio, and Make's notice says current plans and pricing, including the cost of buying credits, remain unchanged.

headline: Vercel Pro swaps fixed usage allotments for $20 of monthly usage credit
details: Announced September 9, 2025: the Pro plan replaces fixed allotments across infrastructure products with $20 of flexible monthly credit, and adds free Viewer seats. Vercel said the new plan would start rolling out automatically in October, with opt-in available immediately, and the Hobby plan stays unchanged.

headline: Kit raises prices for the first time in 12 years; Creator is $39 at 1,000 subscribers
details: Kit's help center calls the update its first price increase in 12 years. For current customers the new pricing applies from the next billing cycle after October 15, 2025; Creator now starts at $39 a month and Pro at $79 for up to 1,000 subscribers. The old prices are not stated in the sources.

headline: Snyk Free plan projects move to weekly recurring tests
details: Snyk announced on September 26, 2024 that recurring tests for Free plan projects would run on a weekly cadence from October 4, 2024. Manual retests in the app or the CLI are not affected.

headline: Thinkific Basic rises from $49 to $54 a month; Start to $109, Grow to $219
details: Thinkific raised Basic, Start, Grow and two legacy plans by about 10% from August 13, 2026, its first subscription increase since 2022. Monthly: Basic $49 to $54, Start $99 to $109, Grow $199 to $219; Expand is unchanged. Existing customers pay it from their first monthly billing cycle or next annual renewal on or after that date; non-profit and discounted accounts are exempt.

headline: Retool Free plan app building moves to Retool-provided AI models
details: Retool's changelog entry of September 28, 2026 says organizations on the Free plan now use Retool-provided models (Retool Mini and Retool Power) for app building. Access to models from other providers is limited to paid plans.

headline: Retool to end Retool Email for Free plan organizations from January 1, 2027
details: Retool announced on September 30, 2026 that from January 1, 2027 Free plan organizations can no longer send email through Retool Email from apps, workflows or automations; the change applies to cloud-hosted Free organizations. Team, Business and Enterprise plans keep access.

headline: Bitwarden removes the Teams Starter plan for new organizations
details: Bitwarden's help center says Teams Starter was removed as an option for new organization creation on June 11, 2024. Existing Teams Starter customers keep their feature set and price.

headline: Bitwarden Premium is now $19.80 a year and Families $47.88, with new features
details: Bitwarden's community announcement said Premium is available at $1.65 a month ($19.80 billed annually) and Families at $3.99 a month ($47.88 billed annually; up to six users, per Thurrott). Existing Premium and early Families 2019 customers get a one-time 25% loyalty discount on their next year of renewal. Previous prices are not stated.

headline: Baserow Cloud Premium becomes $10 per user a month annual, with 5x the rows
details: From August 1, 2024 Baserow Cloud Premium costs $10 per user a month billed annually or $12 monthly, with rows per workspace up from 10,000 to 50,000 and storage from 5 GB to 20 GB. Advanced on monthly billing moved to $22 per user, with no change for yearly cycles. Existing Premium subscribers keep their current price until the end of their billing cycle. Earlier prices are not stated.
unit: per user a month, billed annually (Premium)

headline: FreshBooks raises Lite, Plus and Premium prices for current customers from March 5, 2026
details: FreshBooks' FAQ lists new US prices of $23 (Lite), $43 (Plus) and $70 (Premium) a month, applied to current subscribers on or after March 5, 2026 depending on billing cycle, with at least 30 days' email notice before the billing date. GBP, AUD and EUR Premium prices are listed as unchanged. Old prices are not stated.

headline: Lemon Squeezy cuts payout fees to 0% for US bank accounts and 1% elsewhere
details: Lemon Squeezy announced reduced payout fees on October 22, 2024: 0% per payout for bank accounts in the US and 1% per payout for bank accounts outside the US, starting October 28 (next payout cycle). The post does not state the previous fee amounts.

headline: DeepSeek API starts new pricing and ends off-peak discounts on September 5, 2025
details: With the V3.1 release DeepSeek said new API pricing starts and off-peak discounts end at 16:00 UTC on September 5, 2025; until then the current pricing applied. The page shows the price figures only in an image, so no amounts are given here.

headline: DeepSeek raises V4-Pro and V4-Flash API prices and adds peak and off-peak rates
details: DeepSeek said new API pricing with peak and off-peak rates (off-peak 50% lower than peak) takes effect at 16:00 UTC on August 16, 2026. Reuters, citing a company statement, put the new rates at 50% to 1,100% above current prices depending on model, token type and time of use, effective August 17 (Beijing).

headline: DeepSeek cuts API prices with V4.1-Flash and moves V4-Pro requests to Flash rates
details: DeepSeek's changelog said API prices were reduced with the V4.1-Flash release, new pricing taking effect at 04:00 UTC on September 10, 2026. From September 14, deepseek-v4-pro requests route to V4.1-Flash at Flash rates. Peak and off-peak tiers continue.

headline: DeepSeek to bill search and fetch endpoints at $0.75 per 1,000 calls from October 31, 2026
details: DeepSeek's October 17, 2026 note lists search and fetch endpoints at $0.75 per 1,000 calls each. Server-side tool calls through DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code and Codex are currently free, and billing begins at 16:00 UTC on October 31, 2026.

headline: MailerLite Free plan cut from 500 to 250 subscribers and 12,000 to 2,500 emails a month
details: MailerLite's help center says its Free plan was updated on June 16, 2026 and that all Free accounts are affected: active subscribers fell from 500 to 250 and monthly emails from 12,000 to 2,500. Account users rose from 1 to 2, and new limits include 3 automations and 3 forms.

headline: Render replaces per-member workspace plans with flat Pro at $25 and Scale at $499
details: Render's April 23, 2026 changelog says Pro ($25 a month flat) replaces Professional ($19 per member) and Scale ($499 a month flat) replaces Organization ($29 per member), with unlimited members. Hobby and Pro include less bandwidth than the legacy plans. Workspaces still on legacy plans move automatically on August 1, 2026.

headline: Mixpanel Growth plan now starts at $0 with 1M monthly events; it started at $24 a month
details: In a February 3, 2025 blog post Mixpanel said its Growth plan, which started at $24 a month, now starts at $0 and includes 1M monthly events and 20,000 monthly session replays. The Free plan was unchanged, and customers on the old Growth plan can upgrade to the new plan.
unit: a month, Growth plan starting price

headline: Mattermost v11 cuts Team Edition from 1,000 to 250 users and adds a free Entry edition
details: On August 23, 2025 Mattermost announced that v11 (released October 2025) lowers the Team Edition user limit from 1,000 to 250 and removes GitLab SSO. Paid customers are unaffected. A free Entry edition for small teams has usage caps such as 10,000 messages and 1,000 board cards, some applying in a later release.

headline: Microsoft sells 365 suites without Teams outside the EEA; Teams Enterprise at $5.25
details: From April 1, 2024 Microsoft sold commercial Microsoft 365 and Office 365 suites without Teams outside the EEA and Switzerland, where the suites with Teams were no longer sold to new subscribers, and listed Teams Enterprise at $5.25 per user a month. Existing customers can keep, renew and add seats to current suites.

headline: Microsoft 365 Enterprise suites with Teams return on sale; no-Teams suite prices cut
details: Microsoft's licensing FAQ says that as of November 1, 2025 Enterprise suites with Teams are again available to all customers worldwide in all channels, and prices of Enterprise and Business suites without Teams are reduced. Existing customers get the new pricing at their next renewal; suites with Teams are not affected.

headline: Microsoft 365 Business Basic rises $6 to $7, Business Standard $12.50 to $14 per user
details: Microsoft's commercial price update effective July 1, 2026 also raises Apps for business (includes Excel) from $8.25 to $10.00, Microsoft 365 E3 from $36 to $39 and E5 from $57 to $60 per user a month. Existing customers stay on current pricing until renewal; standalone Teams and Copilot SKUs are excluded.
unit: per user a month, Microsoft 365 Business Basic (USD list price)

headline: Affinity Designer becomes part of the free Affinity app from Canva
details: Canva announced a single Affinity app that combines Designer, Photo and Publisher and is free for individuals, with a Canva account needed to download it. AI tools need a Canva premium plan. The older paid apps stopped receiving updates.

headline: Articulate 360 raises subscription prices: Teams $1,499 and Personal $1,199 a year
details: Articulate said it increased Articulate 360 subscription pricing on July 1, 2024: Teams is $1,499 a year per license and Personal is $1,199 a year; the article does not state the previous prices. The increase applies at renewal, and multi-year plans with locked pricing keep their rate until the contract ends. Teams now includes a Reach 360 starter plan.

headline: Square replaces 18 software subscriptions with Free, Plus ($49) and Premium ($149)
details: Square announced three unified plans in the US: Free ($0), Plus ($49 a month per location) and Premium ($149 a month per location), replacing 18 a la carte subscriptions. In-person rates are 2.5% + 15 cents on Plus and 2.4% + 15 cents on Premium. Most existing US sellers can adopt the new plans.

headline: Supabase cached egress overage drops from $0.09 to $0.03 per GB
details: Supabase split egress into cached and uncached. Paid plans went from a 250 GB combined quota to 250 GB of each type (Free from 5 GB to 5 GB of each), and cached overage is $0.03 per GB while uncached stays $0.09. Accounts move after their next billing cycle reset.
unit: per GB of cached egress overage

headline: Bulutfon stops renting its 6-month and 24-month Santral packages
details: Bulutfon said it would stop renting its 6-month and 24-month cloud PBX (Santral) packages from 1 January 2024 and asked subscribers on those packages to use the 12-month package. Subscribers whose package had not yet expired could keep it until it ended.

headline: Bulutfon Economy yearly package rises from 2,650 TL to 3,790 TL
details: Bulutfon's 2025 price list took effect on 20 January 2025. The yearly Santral packages rose: Advantage from 3,590 to 5,090 TL, Professional from 4,490 to 6,290 TL and Premium from 5,390 to 7,590 TL.

headline: Bulutfon Economy yearly package rises from 3,790 TL to 5,110 TL
details: Bulutfon's 2026 prices were set in its system from 10 January 2026. The yearly Santral packages rose: Advantage from 5,090 to 6,870 TL, Professional from 6,290 to 8,490 TL and Premium from 7,590 to 10,240 TL.

headline: Bulutfon Apsiyon Sanal Santral Plus (0-249 units) rises from 8,400 to 12,000 TL a year
details: Bulutfon updated Apsiyon Sanal Santral Plus yearly prices from 20 January 2026, citing rising costs; the 250-499 unit tier goes from 9,800 to 14,000 TL. New subscriptions use the new prices from 10 January 2026; existing subscribers can keep their current package and price until it expires.

headline: Bulutfon raises yearly number fee from 249 TL to 369 TL per number from 1 December 2026
details: Bulutfon announced on 22 September 2026 that, citing rising costs, the yearly number allocation and usage fee becomes 369 TL per number on 1 December 2026. The post lists the current fee as 249 TL, including VAT and ÖİV, and does not say whether the change covers existing numbers.

headline: Zeplin drops user limits on Free and adds per-project Basic plans with unlimited seats
details: In a 10 June 2024 post Zeplin said the Free plan no longer has user limits (one project, up to 100 screens) and introduced a Basic plan sold per project or project pack at one flat monthly rate with unlimited seats. The post gives no prices or effective date.

headline: Zeplin adds per-seat Advanced plan and retires Team and Organization plans for new buyers
details: From 24 September 2024 Zeplin's Basic plan also comes in 9- and 12-project packs, a per-seat Advanced plan covers up to 50 projects, and Team and Organization became legacy plans no longer sold to new buyers. Existing subscribers keep their terms. The guide gives no prices; Zeplin's pricing page, as read on 22 October 2026, lists Advanced at $12 per seat a month, paid annually.

headline: Sertifier moves new customers to a modular add-on pricing structure
details: In its newsletter of 8 September 2026 Sertifier said it updated its pricing structure and diversified its add-ons so customers can build custom packages. The post says the structure applies only to new customers and any additional accounts created from now on; existing accounts and current plans are unaffected. No prices are given.
